newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican painter, former rebel kidnapped - wife.
newsitem.headline: Mexican painter, former rebel kidnapped - wife.

text.p: Mexican painter Niceforo Urbieta, a former leftist guerrilla granted amnesty in 1977, was kidnapped in the southern state of Oaxaca by suspected security agents, family members said on Thursday.

Urbieta, a former member of a leftist group linked to the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), disappeared on Wednesday after two armed men forced him from his car as he was driving in the state capital Oaxaca, according to his wife, Marcela Vera.
"We think it was a politically motivated kidnapping, because of his participation in political groups in the '70s," she told reporters.
The local attorney general's office said Urbieta was not detained by the local government.

News reports and officials also said on Thursday that the president of the Chiapas state legislature, Mario Lescieur, and three other government officials were being held by peasants blocking roads in the southern state.

The mayor of the city of San Cristobal de las Casas, Rolando Villafuerte, told reporters that Lescieur and the others were kidnapped on Thursday about nine miles (15 km) out of the city by peasants protesting the suspension of electricity in rural areas.

Human rights organisations have said 12 similar kidnappings, allegedly carried out by shadowy paramilitary groups, have been recorded since the June 1996 appearance of the EPR, which has vowed to overthrow the government of President Ernesto Zedillo.
